items.title: Chicago Hotel Strike Hits Marriott and Hilton Hotels During Marathon Weekend
items.summary: Owners, not brands, carry most of the payroll burden. The union's answer is blunt: There is "enough money in this system." But owners see things differently.

items.title: DuVine Cycling’s Case for Experiences You Have to Earn
items.summary: You can visit the most beautiful places in the world and still feel nothing. DuVine's bet is that luxury travelers now want a little friction back, and that the effort is what makes it memorable.

items.title: Delta Air Lines Expects to Absorb $6 Billion Increase in Fuel Costs, Lowers 2026 Profit Outlook
items.summary: Delta still had a profitable third quarter, even as volatile fuel costs are now forcing it to lower its 2026 forecast. The carrier has already accrued $900 million in profit sharing for 2027.

items.title: Accor’s Gulf Hotel Recovery Is A Tale Of Two Markets
items.summary: Leisure demand is carrying Accor’s resorts while city hotels wait for corporate travel to return.

items.title: Announcing Skift Global Forum East 2026: Can the Gulf’s Momentum Hold?
items.summary: A war has turned the Gulf's growth story into an open question. Few leaders have settled how trajectory and traveler trust hold under sustained conflict. Skift Global Forum East puts the people making that call in one room in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Skift Transatlantic Summit: Five Decisions in the Room
items.summary: The transatlantic corridor remains one of travel’s most important markets — and also one of the most exposed to global disruption.

items.title: Higher Airfares Are Here to Stay, but Don’t Expect Airline Profits to Rise
items.summary: Jet fuel costs are hitting new highs, eating into the gains from higher airfares. Delta is expected to be among the few U.S. airlines to see a profit this year.
